item.title: Rabuka confirms Feb 6th 2027 election deadline remains unchanged
item.description: Vijay Narayan , Rashika Kumar · 23/09/2026 Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka says the Government remains committed to holding the next general elections by 6th February next year, with no legal basis for a one-year extension.
item.content:encoded:
Vijay Narayan , Rashika Kumar · 23/09/2026

Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka says the Government remains committed to holding the next general elections by 6th February next year, with no legal basis for a one-year extension.

While responding to questions by fijivillage News in Savusavu, Rabuka confirms thereÂ have been suggestions to extend the deadline for the elections, but it is outside the law.

When questioned about concerns that the constitution process is being rushed, Rabuka says they started talking about the constitution in 2013, when it was decreed into being.

He says everybody were talking about it, and everybody who had spoken about it should have come forward during the consultation.

Rabuka adds the result of the consultation is what they are now taking through Parliament.

He also says that the recommendations in the Constitution Review Commission's report are not the final proposed amendments that will go before Parliament.

He says a Cabinet sub-committee has been deliberating on the Commission's proposed amendments over the past two weeks and making changes.

The Prime Minister says those changes will be the ones that make their way to Parliament. Click here to find the Constitution Review Commission report.

item.title: Savusavu residents to raise climate concerns directly with Kamikamica at FMA Town Hall tonight
item.description: Savusavu residents will have the chance to put their concerns directly to Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica when he will attend the Fijian Media Association Public Town Hall Forum on climate change and environmental issues today. The Pre-COP31 Climate Change Town Hall Forum will be held at Nukubalavu Village in Savusavu from 7pm to 9.30pm today.
item.content:encoded:
Savusavu residents will have the chance to put their concerns directly to Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica when he will attend the Fijian Media Association Public Town Hall Forum on climate change and environmental issues today.

The Pre-COP31 Climate Change Town Hall Forum will be held at Nukubalavu Village in Savusavu from 7pm to 9.30pm today.

The forum, organised by the FMA, will give residents an opportunity to raise concerns about environmental and climate challenges affecting their communities, question Government action and propose practical solutions.

Kamikamica will be joined by Permanent Secretary for the Ministry of Environment Dr Sivendra Michael, other Government officials and experts from regional agencies who will be in Savusavu for the PINA Media Summit.

The discussion will be moderated by fijivillage News Director Vijay Narayan and Fiji Television Manager News Stella Taoi.

Residents are encouraged to share their own experiences, including changes they have observed, challenges affecting their livelihoods and solutions they believe should receive greater attention.

Questions around Government responses and the support needed by communities will also form part of the discussion.

The forum will be livestreamed across participating media platforms, including fijivillage.

It will be held alongside the 8th Pacific Media Summit, hosted by the Fijian Media Association and the Pacific Islands News Association.

The town hall is aimed at bringing community voices into the regional gathering of Pacific journalists and media leaders, while creating a direct platform for public discussion and accountability on climate and environmental issues.

The event is supported by PACMAS and forms part of the Fijian Media Association’s collaborative town hall initiative involving Fiji’s media organisations.

Residents of Savusavu and surrounding communities are being invited to attend and take part in the discussion.

item.title: Family seeks justice after four children hit by vehicle in Tacirua
item.description: One of the four children who was hit by a vehicle in Tacirua earlier this month remains admitted to hospital, while the other three are recovering at their home in Savutalele Settlement in Tacirua. The family is seeking justice and wants Police to take the matter seriously.
item.content:encoded:
One of the four children who was hit by a vehicle in Tacirua earlier this month remains admitted to hospital, while the other three are recovering at their home in Savutalele Settlement in Tacirua.

The family is seeking justice and wants Police to take the matter seriously.

A video of the incident was widely shared on social media, showing a four-wheel-drive vehicle hitting the children as they were walking along the roadside before leaving the scene.

fijivillage News visited the family today, where the children's aunt, Tiare Ofati, showed us the condition of the three children recovering at home.

She says the family is particularly concerned about possible internal injuries as the children continue to recover at home.

Seven-year-old Anna Tepaitaia, a student of Tacirua Primary School, had visible injuries and scars on her leg and around her ribs, while her four-year-old brother also had visible scars on the side of his ribs.

The third child, Charles Ofati, suffered a fractured hand, while the fourth child, Ata Itaia, remains admitted at CWM Children's Hospital.

The aunt says the children were assessed at hospital, but the family was not informed of any internal injuries.

However, she says the children sometimes complain of stomach aches, which continues to concern the family.

The children's aunt says the family has not received any update from Police regarding the driver, who allegedly did not stop after the incident and fled the scene.

She adds that the four children could have lost their lives and is calling for the driver to be held accountable if found responsible.

fijivillage News has sent questions to Police seeking an update on the investigation but is yet to receive a response.

item.title: New Immigration office opens in Nakasi
item.description: People living along the Suva-Nausori corridor will now have easier access to immigration services following the opening of the new Nakasi Immigration Office. The office was officially opened today and will provide key services, including passport applications and citizenship services.
item.content:encoded:
People living along the Suva-Nausori corridor will now have easier access to immigration services following the opening of the new Nakasi Immigration Office.

The office was officially opened today and will provide key services, including passport applications and citizenship services.

Minister for Immigration Viliame Naupoto says the facility is not simply another Government office, but is intended to bring immigration services closer to the people.

Naupoto says the establishment of the office reflects the Government’s commitment to delivering public services in an efficient, accessible and convenient manner.

He says Nakasi was selected because of its strategic location between Suva and Nausori and its development into a major commercial and service hub serving communities along the densely populated corridor.

The Minister says while many citizenship services are now available online, passport applications still require applicants to appear in person for identity verification and the collection of biometric data.

Naupoto has also stressed the standard of service expected from officers working at the new facility.

He says every person who walks through the doors should be treated with dignity, respect, courtesy and professionalism.

The Nakasi office is one of two new Immigration offices being commissioned during the current financial year.

The second office in Rakiraki is nearing completion, while the Ministry also plans to establish additional offices in Sigatoka and Nabouwalu.
